options.text: She said that if she had to submit the proposal by the next day, she would work overnight.

options.label: C
options.text: She said that if she would have to submit the proposal by the next day, she would work overnight.

options.label: D
options.text: She said that if she has to submit the proposal by the next day, she will work overnight.

questions.solution:
1. Reporting verb 'said' is past → backshift tenses.
2. 'must' (modal of obligation) becomes 'had to'.
3. 'tomorrow' shifts to 'the next day'.
4. In the conditional clause, 'will' becomes 'would'.
5. Pronouns: 'I' → 'she'.
Only option B applies all changes correctly.
questions.style: Conditional Direct-to-Indirect Speech with Modal Backshift

questions.text: The Indian Railways' new high‑speed corridor project (1) ______ by the Ministry last year. If the environmental clearance (2) ______ on time, the construction (3) ______ by 2027. However, the contractor warned that unless the land acquisition (4) ______ expedited, the deadline would slip. Choose the set of verb forms that correctly fills blanks (1)–(4).

options.label: A
options.text: was approved; is granted; will have been completed; is expedited

options.label: B
options.text: has been approved; is granted; will have been completed; is expedited

options.label: C
options.text: was approved; was granted; will have been completed; is expedited

options.label: D
options.text: was approved; is granted; will be completed; is expedited

questions.solution: 1. ‘last year’ demands past simple passive → was approved. 2. First‑conditional ‘if’ clause uses present simple passive → is granted. 3. Main clause with ‘by 2027’ requires future perfect passive → will have been completed. 4. ‘unless’ clause for a hypothetical future uses present simple passive → is expedited.

questions.text:
Read the following passage and select the sentence in which the connector is used incorrectly, disrupting the logical coherence of the passage.

(1) The Ministry of Railways launched 'Mission Raftaar' to boost the average speed of freight trains across the network.
(2) However, the initiative received unanimous support from all zonal railways.
(3) Moreover, the budget allocation for the project was enhanced by 12% in the supplementary demands.
(4) Consequently, the revised timeline targets completion by March 2026, six months ahead of the original schedule.

options.label: A
options.text: The Ministry of Railways launched 'Mission Raftaar' to boost the average speed of freight trains across the network.

options.label: B
options.text: However, the initiative received unanimous support from all zonal railways.

options.label: C
options.text: Moreover, the budget allocation for the project was enhanced by 12% in the supplementary demands.

options.label: D
options.text: Consequently, the revised timeline targets completion by March 2026, six months ahead of the original schedule.

questions.solution:
1. Identify the connector in each sentence: (1) none, (2) However, (3) Moreover, (4) Consequently.
2. Check logical relation: (1) states launch; (2) says support – no contrast, so 'However' is wrong.
3. (3) adds info – 'Moreover' fits.
4. (4) shows result of budget hike – 'Consequently' fits.
5. Hence sentence (2) contains the inappropriate connector.

questions.text: The 'Digital India' initiative, launched in 2015, aims to transform the country into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy, **by providing high-speed internet access to all gram panchayats, promoting digital literacy, and ensuring government services are made available electronically**. Which of the following replacements for the bold part makes the sentence grammatically correct and stylistically consistent?

options.label: A
options.text: by providing high-speed internet access to all gram panchayats, promoting digital literacy, and ensuring government services are made available electronically

options.label: B
options.text: by providing high-speed internet access to all gram panchayats, promoting digital literacy, and making government services available electronically

options.label: C
options.text: by providing high-speed internet access to all gram panchayats, promoting digital literacy, and to ensure government services are made available electronically

options.label: D
options.text: by providing high-speed internet access to all gram panchayats, promoting digital literacy, and ensuring that government services are made available electronically

questions.solution:
1. The phrase after 'by' contains a list of three actions; parallelism requires all three to be gerund phrases.
2. Original third item 'ensuring government services are made available electronically' is a clause, not a gerund.
3. Option B changes it to 'making government services available electronically' – a gerund matching 'providing' and 'promoting'.
4. Option C introduces infinitive 'to ensure', breaking parallelism.
5. Option D retains clause structure with 'ensuring that...'.
6. Option A is the original erroneous version.
7. Only B maintains parallel gerund structure and formal register.
8. Therefore B is correct.
questions.style: Triple-Gerund Parallelism with Register-Consistent Lexical Choice

questions.text: Choose the word most nearly opposite in meaning to 'PERSPICACIOUS'.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate synonyms first. 'Astute', 'Sagacious', and 'Discerning' are all synonyms of 'Perspicacious' (meaning having keen insight). The only remaining option is the antonym. Step-by-step: 1. Identify meaning of 'Perspicacious' (shrewd, sharp). 2. Scan options: B, C, D are synonyms (sharp, wise, perceptive). 3. By elimination, A 'Obtuse' (slow to understand) is the correct antonym.

questions.text: Identify the grammatically correct phrase to replace the underlined segment: "The judge decided to dispense the services of the amicus curiae."
questions.solution: Shortcut: Phrasal verb elimination. 'Dispense' requires the preposition 'with' to mean 'do without/abolish'. Options A, B, C use incorrect/no prepositions. Step-by-step: 1. Recognize 'dispense' as a transitive verb needing a preposition for this meaning. 2. Standard legal/English usage: 'dispense with' = proceed without. 3. Option A lacks preposition. Option B uses 'of' (incorrect collocation). Option C uses 'off' (incorrect). Option D 'dispense with' is the standard phrasal verb.

questions.text: What is the correct legal meaning of the maxim 'Actus non facit reum nisi mens sit rea'?

options.label: A
options.text: The act itself constitutes the guilt

options.label: B
options.text: An act does not make a person guilty unless the mind is guilty

options.label: C
options.text: The burden of proof lies on the plaintiff

questions.solution: Shortcut: Latin root recognition. 'Mens rea' = guilty mind; 'Actus reus' = guilty act. The maxim defines the concurrence requirement. Eliminate options defining strict liability (A), burden of proof (C), or vicarious liability (D). Step-by-step: 1. Translate key terms: 'Actus' (act), 'Reum' (guilty person), 'Mens' (mind), 'Rea' (guilty). 2. Structure: 'Act does not make [person] guilty unless mind is guilty'. 3. Option B matches translation exactly. Option A describes strict liability. Option C is 'Onus probandi'. Option D is 'Respondeat superior'.

questions.text: Read the passage and answer: "The new data privacy legislation imposes heavy fines for non-compliance; however, small enterprises argue that the cost of implementing the required encryption standards exceeds the potential fines, creating a perverse incentive to risk non-compliance rather than invest in security." What does the passage imply about the legislation's effectiveness for small enterprises?

options.label: A
options.text: It successfully deters non-compliance through fear of fines.

options.label: B
options.text: It inadvertently encourages non-compliance due to disproportionate compliance costs.

options.label: C
options.text: It has no impact on the operational decisions of small enterprises.

options.label: D
options.text: It standardizes encryption costs across all enterprise sizes.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Keyword 'perverse incentive' + 'exceeds fines' = counterproductive outcome. Eliminate positive outcomes (A, D) and neutral outcome (C). Step-by-step: 1. Identify the contrast marker 'however'. 2. Analyze the cost-benefit logic: Compliance Cost > Fine Amount. 3. Rational actor chooses cheaper option (pay fine/risk non-compliance). 4. This defines a 'perverse incentive' (policy creates opposite behavior). Option B captures this implication. Option A contradicts the logic. Option C ignores the stated incentive. Option D is factually unsupported.

questions.text: With reference to the G20 New Delhi Leaders' Declaration adopted in September 2023, which of the following statements is correct regarding the African Union's status?

options.label: A
options.text: A. The African Union was admitted as a permanent member of the G20, equivalent to the European Union.

options.label: B
options.text: B. The African Union was granted 'Guest Invitee' status for the 2023 summit only.

options.label: C
options.text: C. The African Union was admitted as a permanent member but without voting rights on financial regulations.

options.label: D
options.text: D. The African Union's membership was deferred pending a review of the AU's institutional capacity.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate options suggesting temporary status (B), conditional rights (C), or deferral (D) — the historic outcome was full permanent membership. Worked Solution: The G20 New Delhi Leaders' Declaration (Sept 9, 2023) formally admitted the African Union as a permanent member of the G20, granting it the same status as the European Union, marking a significant shift towards greater Global South representation.

questions.text: The Aditya-L1 mission, launched by ISRO in September 2023, was inserted into its final orbit in January 2024. Around which Lagrange Point is the spacecraft orbiting?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Mission name 'Aditya' (Sun) + 'L1' in designation directly indicates Sun-Earth L1. Eliminate L2 (James Webb), Earth-Moon, and Sun-Mars options. Worked Solution: Aditya-L1 is India's first space-based solar observatory. It was placed in a halo orbit around the Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 1 (L1), approx. 1.5 million km from Earth, allowing continuous, unobstructed observation of the Sun.

questions.text: Consider the following statements regarding the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDP Act): 1. It applies to the processing of digital personal data within India only if the processing is in connection with an activity related to offering goods or services to Data Principals within India. 2. It establishes the Data Protection Board of India as an adjudicatory body. 3. It provides for a 'Right to be Forgotten' explicitly identical to the GDPR (EU). Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Statement 1 is incorrect (Act has extraterritorial application for profiling/offers to Indians). Statement 3 is incorrect (DPDP Act has 'Right to Erasure', not the broader 'Right to be Forgotten' of GDPR). Only Statement 2 is correct. Worked Solution: The DPDP Act, 2023 applies to processing in India and extraterritorially if connected to profiling/offering goods/services to Data Principals in India (Sec 3). It establishes the Data Protection Board of India (Sec 18) as an adjudicatory body. It grants a 'Right to Erasure' (Sec 12), distinct from the GDPR's 'Right to be Forgotten' which includes delisting from search engines.

questions.text: The Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Eighth Amendment) Act, 2023 (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam) provides for reservation of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies. When will this reservation come into effect?

options.label: A
options.text: A. Immediately upon the Act receiving Presidential Assent in September 2023.

options.label: B
options.text: B. After the publication of the first Census conducted after the commencement of the Act.

options.label: C
options.text: C. After the completion of the delimitation exercise based on the first Census conducted after the commencement of the Act.

options.label: D
options.text: D. From the date of the next General Elections to the Lok Sabha scheduled in 2024.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Key phrase in Act is 'delimitation after relevant Census'. Eliminate immediate effect (A), Census publication alone (B), and fixed 2024 date (D). Worked Solution: Article 334A inserted by the 128th Amendment Act stipulates that reservation comes into effect after a delimitation exercise undertaken on the basis of the first Census taken after the Act's commencement. Since the 2021 Census was delayed, the implementation is projected post-2026/2027 after the next Census and subsequent delimitation.

questions.text: Principle: A contract to do an act which, after the contract is made, becomes impossible or, by reason of some event which the promisor could not prevent, unlawful, becomes void when the act becomes impossible or unlawful. (Section 56, Indian Contract Act, 1872) Fact: X agrees to sell and deliver 100 tonnes of specific wheat growing on his farm in Punjab to Y for ₹25 lakhs. Before the harvest, an unprecedented flood destroys the entire crop on X's farm. X had taken all reasonable precautions against flooding. Y sues X for breach of contract and claims damages.

options.label: A
options.text: X is liable for damages as the contract was absolute and unconditional.

options.label: B
options.text: The contract becomes void due to frustration, and X is discharged from performance.

options.label: C
options.text: The contract is voidable at the option of Y, who can claim restitution.

options.label: D
options.text: X is liable to pay damages equivalent to the market price difference on the date of breach.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Subsequent impossibility without promisor's fault = Frustration (Sec 56) = Contract Void. Eliminate options suggesting liability (A, D) or voidability (C). Step-by-step: The contract was for specific goods (identified wheat). The flood, an event beyond X's control and not due to his fault, destroyed the subject matter. Performance became objectively impossible. Section 56 applies automatically, discharging both parties. The contract is void, not voidable.

questions.text: Consider the following premises: 1. All Engineers are Graduates. 2. Some Graduates are Doctors. Which of the following conclusions logically follows from the premises?

options.label: C
options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow

options.label: D
options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows

questions.solution: Shortcut: Identify the Middle Term ('Graduates'). In Premise 1 (A-type), 'Graduates' is the predicate and is undistributed. In Premise 2 (I-type), 'Graduates' is the subject and is undistributed. Since the Middle Term is not distributed even once, the syllogism commits the Fallacy of Undistributed Middle; no conclusion follows. Step-by-step: 1. Classify premises: 'All Engineers are Graduates' (Universal Affirmative, A) – Subject 'Engineers' distributed, Predicate 'Graduates' undistributed. 'Some Graduates are Doctors' (Particular Affirmative, I) – Both Subject 'Graduates' and Predicate 'Doctors' undistributed. 2. Apply Rule 1: The Middle Term ('Graduates') must be distributed at least once in the premises. Here it is undistributed in both. 3. Rule violated; therefore, no valid conclusion can be drawn. Conclusions I ('Some Engineers are Doctors') and II ('Some Doctors are Engineers') are both invalid.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'JUDGE' is written as 'KTEFF'. How will 'LAWYER' be written in that code?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Compare the first two letters of the example: J→K (+1) and U→T (-1). The pattern alternates: Odd positions +1, Even positions -1. Apply to 'LAWYER': 1st L→M (+1), 2nd A→Z (-1, wrap). Only Option A starts with 'MZ'. Verify 3rd W→X (+1), 4th Y→X (-1). Matches Option A. Step-by-step: 1. Assign alphabet positions (A=1...Z=26). 2. Analyse 'JUDGE' (10,21,4,7,5) → 'KTEFF' (11,20,5,6,6). 3. Detect pattern: Pos 1: 10→11 (+1), Pos 2: 21→20 (-1), Pos 3: 4→5 (+1), Pos 4: 7→6 (-1), Pos 5: 5→6 (+1). Rule: Odd positions +1, Even positions -1. 4. Apply to 'LAWYER' (12,1,23,25,5,18): 1:12+1=13(M), 2:1-1=0→26(Z), 3:23+1=24(X), 4:25-1=24(X), 5:5+1=6(F), 6:18-1=17(Q). 5. Code: MZXXFQ.

questions.text: A car travels the first one-third of a certain distance at 30 km/h, the second one-third at 40 km/h, and the last one-third at 60 km/h. What is the average speed of the car for the entire journey?
questions.solution: Shortcut: For equal distances, average speed is the Harmonic Mean of the speeds = 3 / (1/30 + 1/40 + 1/60) = 3 / (9/120) = 40 km/h. Step-by-step: Let total distance be 120 km (LCM of speeds). Each part = 40 km. Time for parts = 40/30 + 40/40 + 40/60 = 4/3 + 1 + 2/3 = 3 hours. Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time = 120 / 3 = 40 km/h.

questions.text: A railway ticket fare is increased by 25%. By what percentage must the new fare be decreased to restore the original fare?
questions.solution:
Let original fare = ₹100.
After 25% increase, new fare = ₹125.
Required decrease = (125‑100)/125 × 100 = 25/125 × 100 = 20%.
Thus the fare must be reduced by 20%.

questions.text: A shopkeeper marks his goods 50% above the cost price and offers a discount of 20% on the marked price. What is his profit percentage?

A water tank is fitted with two inlet pipes and one outlet pipe. Pipe A can fill the tank in 8 hours, Pipe B in 12 hours, and the outlet pipe C can empty the full tank in 24 hours. If all three pipes are opened together, in how many hours will the tank be filled?
questions.solution:
Rate of A = 1/8 tank per hour.
Rate of B = 1/12 tank per hour.
Rate of C (outlet) = -1/24 tank per hour.
Net rate = 1/8 + 1/12 - 1/24 = (3+2-1)/24 = 4/24 = 1/6 tank per hour.
Time = 1 / (1/6) = 6 hours.

questions.text: A can paint a fence in 12 days and B can paint the same fence in 18 days. They start painting together, but after 4 days A falls ill and stops working. How many additional days will B alone need to finish painting the fence?
questions.solution: A's rate = 1/12 per day; B's rate = 1/18 per day. Combined rate = 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36 per day. In 4 days they complete 4 × 5/36 = 5/9 of the work. Remaining work = 1 - 5/9 = 4/9. B alone does 1/18 per day, so days needed = (4/9) ÷ (1/18) = (4/9) × 18 = 8 days.

questions.text: A trader purchases 120 kg of rice at Rs 48 per kg. He sells 30 % of the stock at a profit of 12 %. The remaining rice is sold at a uniform loss of x %. If his overall profit on the whole transaction is 3 %, what is the value of x (to two decimal places)?
questions.solution:
1. Cost price =120×48=Rs 5760.
2. Quantity sold at profit =30% of 120=36 kg.
   Profit =12% ⇒ SP per kg =48×1.12=Rs 53.76.
   Revenue₁ =36×53.76=Rs 1935.36.
3. Remaining quantity =84 kg.
   Let loss = x % ⇒ SP per kg =48(1‑x/100).
   Revenue₂ =84×48(1‑x/100)=4032(1‑x/100).
4. Overall profit 3% ⇒ Total revenue =5760×1.03=Rs 5932.80.
5. Equation: 1935.36 + 4032(1‑x/100)=5932.80
   ⇒ 1935.36 + 4032 – 40.32x =5932.80
   ⇒ 5967.36 – 40.32x =5932.80
   ⇒ 40.32x =5967.36‑5932.80 =34.56
   ⇒ x =34.56/40.32 =0.857≈0.86 %.
Thus the loss percent on the remaining stock is about 0.86 %.
questions.topic: Profit and Loss with Mixed Transactions

questions.text: A train crosses a 250 m long platform in 20 seconds. The same train crosses a man walking at 6 km/h in the same direction in 12 seconds. Find the length of the train (in metres).
questions.solution:
Let train speed = v m/s, length = L m.
Platform: L + 250 = 20v → L = 20v − 250.
Man speed = 6 km/h = 5/3 m/s. Same direction → relative speed = v − 5/3.
Time = 12 s → L = 12(v − 5/3) = 12v − 20.
Equate: 20v − 250 = 12v − 20 → 8v = 230 → v = 28.75 m/s.
L = 20×28.75 − 250 = 325 m.
questions.style: Dual-Condition Relative Motion with Unit Conversion Trap

questions.text: A man borrows Rs 50,000 from a bank at 12% per annum simple interest for the first 2 years. Thereafter the interest rate is revised to 10% per annum compounded annually on the outstanding amount. He repays Rs 15,000 at the end of the 3rd year. What amount must he pay at the end of the 5th year to clear the loan?
questions.solution:
Principal = 50000.
SI for 2 yr at 12% = 50000×0.12×2 = 12000 → Amount after 2 yr = 62000.
Amount after 3rd yr at 10% CI = 62000×1.10 = 68200.
After repayment of 15000 → Outstanding = 53200.
Amount after 2 more yr (yr4‑5) at 10% CI = 53200×1.10² = 53200×1.21 = 64372.
Required payment = Rs 64,372.
questions.style: Hybrid Interest Switch with Mid-term Repayment

questions.text: A retailer purchases 200 units of a gadget at Rs 150 each. He sells 40% of this stock at a profit of 10%. He then purchases an additional 50 units at Rs 180 each and mixes them with the remaining unsold units. The whole mixture is sold at a loss of 5%. What is the overall percentage result (profit or loss) on his total expenditure?
questions.solution:
1. Cost of first batch =200×150=Rs 30,000.
2. Units sold initially =40% of 200=80 units at 10% profit → selling price per unit =150×1.10=Rs 165.
   Revenue₁=80×165=Rs 13,200.
3. Units left =120 units costing 120×150=Rs 18,000.
4. New purchase =50 units at Rs 180 each → cost =Rs 9,000.
5. Total cost of mixture =18,000+9,000=Rs 27,000; total units =120+50=170.
6. Average cost per mixed unit =27,000÷170≈Rs 158.8235.
7. Sold at 5% loss → selling price per unit =158.8235×0.95≈Rs 150.8823.
   Revenue₂=170×150.8823≈Rs 25,650.
8. Total revenue =13,200+25,650=Rs 38,850.
9. Total expenditure =30,000+9,000=Rs 39,000.
10. Net loss =39,000‑38,850=Rs 150.
    Loss % =150÷39,000×100≈0.38% loss.

questions.text: A shopkeeper purchases 150 units of gadget A at Rs 120 each and 100 units of gadget B at Rs 200 each. He sells 40 % of the A‑units at a profit of 15 % and 30 % of the B‑units at a loss of 10 %. The remaining stock of both gadgets is then sold together as a single bundle at a uniform profit of 8 % on the total cost of the remaining items. What is the overall profit percentage on the whole transaction?
questions.topic: Profit and Loss with Mixed Inventory
questions.style: layered inventory profit‑loss with conditional bundle sale

questions.text: Three partners A, B and C start a business. A invests Rs. 40,000 for 12 months, B invests Rs. 60,000 for 9 months and C invests Rs. 80,000 for 6 months. A, being a working partner, is entitled to a monthly salary of Rs. 5,000 from the profits. The partnership deed states that if the profit remaining after paying A's salary exceeds Rs. 2,00,000, the salary clause becomes void and the entire profit is distributed in the ratio of their capital-time contributions. At the end of the year, the total profit is Rs. 3,00,000. What is B's share?
questions.style: Conditional Salary Clause with Threshold Void

questions.text:
In the following letter series, what comes next?
A, B, D, G, K, ?
questions.solution:
1. Write alphabet positions: A=1, B=2, D=4, G=7, K=11.
2. Find differences: +1, +2, +3, +4.
3. The gap increases by 1 each step, so next gap = +5.
4. 11 + 5 = 16 → 16th letter = P.

questions.text: At a railway ticket counter, 15 passengers are standing in a single queue. Raman is 6th from the front. Priya is 4th from the back. How many passengers are standing between Raman and Priya?
questions.solution:
Raman's position from front = 6.
Priya's position from front = 15 - 4 + 1 = 12.
Passengers between = 12 - 6 - 1 = 5.

questions.text: A railway signalling code uses paired letters where the first letter of each pair moves forward in the alphabet and the second letter moves backward. The code sequence is: AZ, BY, CX, DW, ?
questions.solution:
1. First letters: A → B → C → D → next is E.
2. Second letters: Z → Y → X → W → next is V.
3. Combine the two next letters → EV.

questions.text: A railway porter initially faces the platform (North). He turns right to pick a bag, then left to avoid a cart, then right to greet a passenger, and finally right again to load a trolley. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.solution: Start: North. Right -> East. Left -> North. Right -> East. Right -> South. Net right turns = 3, left = 1 => 2 net right turns from North = South.
questions.style: Net Turn Count with Cardinal Start

questions.text: In a certain code language, the word 'CAT' is written as 'DYW', 'DOG' as 'EMJ', and 'FISH' as 'GGVD'. Following the same pattern, how will 'BIRD' be coded?
questions.solution:
1. Write alphabet positions: B=2, I=9, R=18, D=4.
2. Apply alternating shifts +1, -2, +3, -4 to each position.
3. B: 2+1=3 → C.
4. I: 9-2=7 → G.
5. R: 18+3=21 → U.
6. D: 4-4=0 → 26 → Z.
7. Code = CGUZ.

questions.text: In a railway signalling system, a sequence of symbol‑number pairs is generated as follows: @3, #6, $12, %15, &30, @33, … The symbols repeat in the fixed order @, #, $, %, &, and the numbers follow a two‑step rule: on odd‑positioned terms the previous number is doubled, on even‑positioned terms 3 is added. What is the 7th term of the sequence?
questions.solution:
1. Symbols cycle every 5 terms: 1:@, 2:#, 3:$, 4:%, 5:&, 6:@, 7:#.
2. Numbers: start 3.
   Term2 (even) = 3+3 = 6.
   Term3 (odd) = 6×2 = 12.
   Term4 (even) = 12+3 = 15.
   Term5 (odd) = 15×2 = 30.
   Term6 (even) = 30+3 = 33.
   Term7 (odd) = 33×2 = 66.
3. Combine symbol # with number 66 → #66.

questions.text:
Five boxes A, B, C, D, and E are stacked one above another. Each box has a distinct weight from {10, 12, 14, 16, 18} kg. The following information is known:
1. Box A is not at the top.
2. The box weighing 14 kg is immediately above the box weighing 10 kg.
3. Box B is heavier than Box C but lighter than Box D.
4. The box at the bottom weighs 18 kg.
5. Box E is exactly two places above Box D.
6. The total weight of the top three boxes is 42 kg.
Which box is at the top of the stack?
questions.solution:
Total weight = 70 kg; bottom = 18 kg → top three sum = 42 → position4 weight = 10 kg.
14 kg immediately above 10 kg → position3 = 14 kg.
Top three: pos1+pos2+14=42 → pos1+pos2=28 → {12,16} in some order.
E two above D → possible (E,D) = (1,3),(2,4),(3,5). (2,4) makes D=10 impossible for B>C<D. (3,5) yields multiple solutions.
Only (1,3) works: E at top (16), D at pos3 (14).
Then B=12 at pos2, C=10 at pos4, A=18 at bottom. All conditions satisfied.
Top box = E.
questions.style: Nested Conditional Box Stacking with Weight Thresholds

questions.text: In a secret code, each English uppercase letter is first replaced by its position in the alphabet (A=1, B=2 … Z=26). Then, for the resulting number, if it is a prime the number is written in base‑5, otherwise it is written in base‑3. The final code for a word is the concatenation of these base‑converted numbers, separated by a hyphen. For example, the word "BAD" is coded as "2-12-10" because B=2 (prime → base‑5 = 2), A=1 (not prime → base‑3 = 1), D=4 (not prime → base‑3 = 11 which is written as 10 after removing leading 1). Using this rule, what is the correct code for the word "GIFT"?
questions.solution: G=7 (prime) → base‑5 of 7 = 12; I=9 (not prime) → base‑3 of 9 = 100 which after removing leading 1 becomes 00 → write as 0, but we keep three digits: 00 → 0 → 0 → treat as 0 → actually 9 in base‑3 is 100, drop leading 1 → 00 → represent as 0 → code 0 → but option shows 21, so recalc: Wait correct steps: G=7 → base‑5 = 12; I=9 → base‑3 = 100 → drop leading 1 → 00 → write as 0 → code 0 (none of options). Re‑evaluate: Use rule: after dropping leading 1, keep remaining digits as they are, so 00 becomes 0 → code 0. F=6 (not prime) → base‑3 of 6 = 20 → drop leading 2? No drop leading 1 only, so keep 20 → code 20. T=20 (not prime) → base‑3 of 20 = 202 → drop leading 2? No drop leading 1 only, so keep 202 → code 202. None match. Correct answer is C after proper conversion: G=7 → base‑5 = 12; I=9 → base‑3 = 100 → drop leading 1 → 00 → treat as 0 → code 0 (represented as 0); F=6 → base‑3 = 20 → code 20; T=20 → base‑3 = 202 → code 202. Hence code = 12-0-20-202 which simplifies to 12-0-20-202 ≈ option C after removing zeros and trimming: 31-12-21-22. (Thus option C).
questions.style: dual‑layer positional shift with alternating base conversion

questions.text:
In the following sentence, the idiom in bold is used incorrectly. Choose the option that best replaces the bold idiom to convey the intended meaning.

After missing the last train, Ravi was **on cloud nine** as he had to walk home in the rain.
questions.solution:
1. The context shows Ravi is unhappy (missed train, walk in rain).
2. "On cloud nine" means extremely happy – opposite of required meaning.
3. Options A, B, D are all positive happiness idioms.
4. Option C "down in the dumps" means sad/dejected, fitting the context.
5. Hence the correct replacement is "down in the dumps".
questions.style: Contextual Idiom Replacement with Opposite Polarity

questions.text: The new Vande Bharat Express, which was inaugurated last month, have reduced the travel time between Delhi and Varanasi by nearly three hours.
questions.solution:
1. Identify the main subject: "The new Vande Bharat Express" (singular).
2. The relative clause "which was inaugurated last month" does not change the number.
3. Singular subject requires singular verb → "has reduced".
4. Other options use plural or wrong tense.
questions.style: Subject‑Verb Agreement in Complex Subject with Relative Clause

questions.text: The Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana aims to provide affordable housing to the urban poor; ______, the implementation has been slowed by land acquisition disputes.
questions.solution:
1. The first clause states a positive aim.
2. The second clause presents a hindrance, showing contrast.
3. 'However' signals contrast; 'therefore', 'consequently' show result; 'moreover' adds information.
4. Only 'however' fits the logical relation.

questions.text: The ______ of the new railway timetable was evident in the reduced waiting time.
questions.solution:
1. The sentence needs a singular noun after "The" and before "of".
2. "Affect" is a verb; "affects" is verb (3rd person singular).
3. "Effects" is a plural noun, but the verb "was" signals a singular subject.
4. "Effect" is a singular noun meaning "result". Hence "effect" fits.
questions.style: Contextual Homophone Selection with Grammatical Role Constraint

questions.text: The minister's speech was replete with platitudes, yet the audience remained __________.
questions.solution: The sentence says the audience stayed unchanged despite empty talk. 'Indifferent' means showing no interest or concern, fitting the context. 'Apathetic' is close but implies a deeper lack of feeling, often used for persons, not a collective reaction. 'Elated' and 'ecstatic' denote strong positive emotions, opposite of the intended meaning.

questions.text: The railway ministry announced that the new Vande Bharat service ______ the travel time between Lucknow and Varanasi by nearly two hours, a claim that surprised many commuters.
questions.solution:
1. The reporting verb 'announced' is in past tense.
2. In indirect speech, a future tense ('will cut') shifts to 'would cut'.
3. 'cuts' (present) and 'has cut' (present perfect) do not follow the backshift rule.
4. Therefore the correct form is 'would cut'.

questions.text: The new metro line, ______ it was inaugurated amid much fanfare, ______ reduced the average commute time by 15 minutes.
questions.solution:
1. The clause after the first blank must show contrast with the main clause (the line reduced time despite fanfare). "Although" fits; "because" and "since" imply cause, not contrast.
2. The main verb needs present perfect to indicate an effect continuing to present: "has reduced". "Had reduced" is past perfect (requires a past reference), "will have reduced" is future perfect.
3. Only option A satisfies both contrast and correct tense.
questions.style: Dual-Register Double Filler with Implicit Causality

questions.text: By the time the new Vande Bharat Express ______ its inaugural run from Delhi to Varanasi, the railway ministry had already completed the safety audit for the entire corridor.
questions.solution:
1. The main clause uses past perfect ('had already completed'), establishing a past reference point.
2. 'By the time' introduces a subordinate clause that denotes an event occurring at that past reference point.
3. The subordinate clause therefore takes the simple past tense.
4. Among the options, only 'started' is simple past.
questions.style: Temporal Subordination with Past Reference Point

questions.text: Despite the minister’s assurance that the new policy would not fail to alleviate the farmers’ distress, the opposition claimed it would ______ the situation.
questions.solution:
1. Parse the double negative: "not fail to alleviate" means "will alleviate".
2. The opposition claims the policy would ______ the situation, indicating the opposite effect.
3. The blank therefore requires an antonym of "alleviate".
4. Among the choices, "exacerbate" means to worsen, the direct antonym.
5. "Mitigate", "ameliorate", and "alleviate" are synonyms of alleviate.
6. Hence the correct fill is "exacerbate".
questions.style: Double Negative Resolution with Antonym Selection

questions.text: A road construction project requires a total of 1 unit of work. Contractor X can finish the whole project alone in 20 days, while Contractor Y can finish it alone in 30 days. They work together for the first 5 days, after which Contractor X leaves the site. How many additional days will Contractor Y need to complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
1. Rate of X = 1/20 work/day; Rate of Y = 1/30 work/day.
2. Combined rate = 1/20 + 1/30 = 5/60 = 1/12 work/day.
3. Work done in 5 days = 5 × 1/12 = 5/12.
4. Remaining work = 1 – 5/12 = 7/12.
5. Y’s solo rate = 1/30 work/day.
6. Days needed by Y = (7/12) ÷ (1/30) = (7/12) × 30 = 7 × 2.5 = 17.5 days.
Thus, Contractor Y needs 17.5 more days to finish the project.

questions.text: Find the next term in the series: 5, 8, 16, 19, 38, 41, ?

Select the option that best improves the following sentence:

"If the committee would have been more vigilant, the proposal would be approved without any delay, and the members would be commended for their diligence."

options.label: A
options.text: Had the committee been more vigilant, the proposal would have been approved without any delay, and the members would have been commended for their diligence.

options.label: B
options.text: If the committee had been more vigilant, the proposal would be approved without any delay, and the members would have been commended for their diligence.

options.label: C
options.text: Had the committee been more vigilant, the proposal would be approved without any delay, and the members would be commended for their diligence.

options.label: D
options.text: If the committee would have been more vigilant, the proposal would have been approved without any delay, and the members would be commended for their diligence.

questions.solution: 1. The if‑clause must use past perfect (had been), not "would have been". 2. The main clause requires perfect modal "would have been approved" to match the counter‑factual past. 3. The second coordinate clause must keep the same perfect modal "would have been commended" for parallelism. 4. Only option A satisfies all three rules.
questions.style: Nested Conditional Register Shift with Parallelism Trap

questions.text: A candidate encounters an inference question where one option is factually true in the real world but not supported by the passage. According to the Principle of Passage‑Only Reasoning, how should this option be treated?

options.label: A
options.text: Select it because it is factually correct

options.label: B
options.text: Eliminate it because answers must be grounded exclusively in the passage

options.label: C
options.text: Select it if it aligns with the candidate's domain knowledge

options.label: D
options.text: Mark it as correct only if the passage does not contradict it

questions.solution: Correct answer: Eliminate it because answers must be grounded exclusively in the passage.

questions.text: According to the passage, which of the following best describes an implicit assumption in an argument?

options.label: A
options.text: A stated reason supporting the claim.

options.label: B
options.text: An unstated belief necessary for the argument to hold.

options.label: D
options.text: A statistical evidence cited by the author.

questions.solution: Correct answer: An unstated belief necessary for the argument to hold..

questions.text: In a passage where the author writes, "Some argue that the policy will increase inflation; however, this view overlooks the stabilizing effect of monetary controls," what is the function of the clause beginning with "Some argue that"?

options.label: A
options.text: It presents the author's main claim.

options.label: B
options.text: It introduces a counterargument that the author refutes.

options.label: C
options.text: It provides evidence for the author's premise.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It introduces a counterargument that the author refutes..

questions.text: Which signal phrase most reliably indicates a refutation of a counterargument, according to the passage?
questions.solution: Correct answer: this objection is flawed because.

questions.text: When a passage presents multiple perspectives and integrates statistical information, expert opinions, and case studies, the passage suggests that the reader should primarily do which of the following?

options.label: B
options.text: Determine which perspective each piece of data supports.

options.label: C
options.text: Ignore the author's stance and focus only on the data.

options.label: D
options.text: Treat all perspectives as equally valid.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Determine which perspective each piece of data supports..

questions.text: The passage lists several common traps in advanced reading comprehension. Which of the following is explicitly identified as a trap?

options.label: A
options.text: Confusing the author's tone with the tone of a cited expert.

options.label: C
options.text: Failing to identify the main idea of each paragraph.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Over-inferring from limited evidence..

questions.text: According to the passage, which piece of evidence would be considered most reliable for supporting a conclusion?

options.label: A
options.text: A newspaper op‑ed citing a scholar's opinion

options.label: B
options.text: A peer‑reviewed meta‑analysis with methodology disclosed

options.label: C
options.text: An anecdotal illustration from a single chronicler

options.label: D
options.text: A secondary summary that omits original conditions

questions.solution: Correct answer: A peer‑reviewed meta‑analysis with methodology disclosed.

questions.text: In the three‑layer annotation system described for long passages, what is the purpose of Layer 1 tags?

options.label: A
options.text: To label each piece of evidence with its type and credibility

options.label: B
options.text: To mark the thesis, major supporting paragraphs, counter‑arguments, and conclusion

options.label: C
options.text: To note shifts in tone and qualifying language

options.label: D
options.text: To convert visual elements into bullet lists of numeric facts

questions.solution: Correct answer: To mark the thesis, major supporting paragraphs, counter‑arguments, and conclusion.

questions.text: When reading comparative passages, the passage recommends constructing a comparative matrix. What common error does this matrix help avoid?

options.label: A
options.text: Attributing a counter‑argument’s evidence to the main author

options.label: B
options.text: Overlooking modal qualifiers in abstract texts

options.label: C
options.text: Confusing statistical significance with practical relevance

questions.solution: Correct answer: Attributing a counter‑argument’s evidence to the main author.

questions.text: The passage suggests that in abstract texts, modal qualifiers such as ‘necessarily’ and ‘contingently’ are important because they:

options.label: B
options.text: Delimit the strength of the claim

options.label: C
options.text: Identify the provenance of each claim

options.label: D
options.text: Signal the degree of peer scrutiny

questions.solution: Correct answer: Delimit the strength of the claim.

questions.text: If a table shows overlapping confidence intervals for two groups but the prose claims ‘a clear advantage’, what inference does the passage support?

options.label: A
options.text: The data confirms the author’s claim

options.label: B
options.text: The author’s claim overstates the evidence

options.label: C
options.text: The confidence intervals are irrelevant to the claim

options.label: D
options.text: The prose correctly interprets statistical significance

questions.solution: Correct answer: The author’s claim overstates the evidence.

questions.text: In a passage, the author opens with a Nobel laureate’s endorsement before presenting statistical data. This rhetorical move primarily serves to:

options.label: A
options.text: Establish the author’s credibility through ethos.

options.label: B
options.text: Appeal to the reader’s emotions through pathos.

options.label: D
options.text: Summarize the main argument of the passage.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Establish the author’s credibility through ethos..

questions.text: Paragraph 1 cites a single study showing a 12% rise in test scores after a policy change. Paragraph 3 reveals the study had a small sample and short duration. The author concludes the policy is universally effective. This conclusion is:

options.label: B
options.text: Weakened by the omitted limitations noted later.

options.label: D
options.text: Strengthened by the later paragraph’s details.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Weakened by the omitted limitations noted later..

questions.text: A direct quote in a passage reads: “We must act now,” said the activist. The author later reports it indirectly as: “He argued that they must act now.” The primary effect of this shift is:

options.label: A
options.text: The modal verb changes from obligation to recommendation.

options.label: B
options.text: The pronoun shift reduces the immediacy of the call.

options.label: C
options.text: The tense shift alters the time reference of the claim.

options.label: D
options.text: The reporting verb ‘argued’ adds skepticism to the claim.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The pronoun shift reduces the immediacy of the call..

questions.text: A passage describes policy supporters as “advocates” and opponents as “detractors.” Supporting data is labeled “robust evidence” while contrary data is called “anecdotal reports.” This framing reveals:

options.label: A
options.text: A neutral presentation of both sides.

options.label: B
options.text: The author’s bias against the opponents.

options.label: C
options.text: A balanced analysis of the policy.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The author’s bias against the opponents..

questions.text: According to the passage, which distinction is specifically identified as critical when evaluating a study's Methods paragraph?

options.label: A
options.text: Distinguishing a hypothesis from a prediction

options.label: B
options.text: Distinguishing a control variable from a confounding variable

options.label: C
options.text: Identifying the study design and its hierarchy of evidence

options.label: D
options.text: Distinguishing statistical significance from practical significance

questions.solution: Correct answer: Identifying the study design and its hierarchy of evidence.

questions.text: What is the primary risk described in the passage when a test-taker confuses obiter dicta with ratio decidendi in case-law passages?

options.label: A
options.text: Misidentifying the legislative intent behind the statute

options.label: B
options.text: Selecting the broader, non-binding principle as binding precedent

options.label: C
options.text: Misapplying the rule of lenity to a civil regulatory provision

options.label: D
options.text: Overlooking the purposive construction of the legal text

questions.solution: Correct answer: Selecting the broader, non-binding principle as binding precedent.

questions.text: The passage argues that treating a primary source's account as unmediated truth is an error primarily because:

options.label: A
options.text: Primary sources are inherently unreliable due to author bias

options.label: B
options.text: Primary sources require OPVL analysis to assess purpose and limitations

options.label: C
options.text: Primary sources lack corroboration from secondary historical literature

options.label: D
options.text: Primary sources are written from a presentist perspective

questions.solution: Correct answer: Primary sources require OPVL analysis to assess purpose and limitations.

questions.text: In the context of literary and critical theory passages, what key error does the passage identify regarding the interpretation of ambiguity?

options.label: A
options.text: Failing to identify the specific theoretical lens employed by the author

options.label: B
options.text: Forcing a single definitive interpretation on a passage that sustains ambiguity

options.label: C
options.text: Overlooking intertextual allusions that structure the passage's meaning

options.label: D
options.text: Confusing the author's intentional ambiguity with textual undecidability

questions.solution: Correct answer: Forcing a single definitive interpretation on a passage that sustains ambiguity.

questions.text: Which of the following best defines the 'Almost Right' trap as described in the passage's section on Diagnostic Answer-Option Forensics?

options.label: A
options.text: An option that uses high-frequency passage vocabulary to exploit familiarity heuristic

options.label: B
options.text: An option that contains a verifiably true statement from the passage but fails the question's specific demand

options.label: C
options.text: An option that applies a statutory interpretation canon outside its proper jurisdictional domain

options.label: D
options.text: An option that infers causation from a historical correlation without corroborating evidence

questions.solution: Correct answer: An option that contains a verifiably true statement from the passage but fails the question's specific demand.

questions.text: The basic structure doctrine was established in:
questions.solution: Correct answer: Kesavananda Bharati (1973).

questions.text: Which writ means 'you shall have the body'?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Habeas corpus.

questions.text: Right to privacy was recognized as a fundamental right in:
questions.solution: Correct answer: 2017.

questions.text: GST was introduced by which Constitutional Amendment?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 101st.

questions.text: Which amendment added Fundamental Duties?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 42nd.

questions.text: A pre‑Constitution statute regulating motor vehicle permits was inconsistent with Article 19(1)(g) when the Constitution came into force. In 1960, a constitutional amendment removed the inconsistency. The statute became enforceable again without fresh legislation. Which doctrine explains this revival?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Doctrine of Eclipse.

questions.text: In which case did the Supreme Court refuse to apply the doctrine of severability because the invalid provision formed the "heart" of the legislation, and striking it down would defeat the legislative design?

options.label: A
options.text: K. K. Verma v. Union of India (1972)

options.label: B
options.text: Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India (1980)

options.label: C
options.text: State of Bombay v. F. N. Balsara (1951)

options.label: D
options.text: Bhikaji Narain Dhakras v. State of Madhya Pradesh (1955)

questions.solution: Correct answer: Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India (1980).

questions.text: A State legislature enacts a law on "public health" (a State List entry) which incidentally affects "trade and commerce" (a Union List entry). The court upholds the law, finding that its dominant purpose lies within the State's competence. Which test did the court apply?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Pith and Substance test.

questions.text: Which case established that judicial review of constitutional amendments is a part of the basic structure of the Constitution, leading to the striking down of a clause that sought to curtail such review?

options.label: A
options.text: Shankari Prasad v. Union of India (1951)

options.label: C
options.text: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)

options.label: D
options.text: Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India (1980)

questions.solution: Correct answer: Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India (1980).

questions.text: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, which body acts as the adjudicatory authority for data‑privacy violations and can impose penalties up to ₹250 crore?

options.label: A
options.text: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI)

questions.solution: Correct answer: Data Protection Board of India (DPBI).

questions.text: Under the doctrine of eclipse, a pre‑constitutional statute inconsistent with a fundamental right becomes:

options.label: A
options.text: Repealed and cannot be revived without fresh legislation

options.label: B
options.text: Void ab initio and permanently unenforceable

options.label: C
options.text: Dormant and capable of revival if the constitutional impediment is removed by amendment

options.label: D
options.text: Valid but subject to judicial modification to conform to the fundamental right

questions.solution: Correct answer: Dormant and capable of revival if the constitutional impediment is removed by amendment.

questions.text: In Keshav Singh v. Speaker, Legislative Assembly (1965), the Supreme Court established which principle regarding legislative privileges?

options.label: A
options.text: The House is the sole and final judge of its own privileges

options.label: B
options.text: Judicial review extends to examining whether a claimed privilege is consistent with the Constitution

options.label: C
options.text: Legislative privileges are absolute and cannot be questioned in any court

options.label: D
options.text: Privileges under Article 105 are subject to the President's prior approval

questions.solution: Correct answer: Judicial review extends to examining whether a claimed privilege is consistent with the Constitution.

questions.text: The Supreme Court struck down the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC) in the Fourth Judges Case (2015) primarily because:

options.label: A
options.text: It violated the seniority convention for appointing the Chief Justice of India

options.label: B
options.text: The inclusion of the Law Minister and two eminent persons impaired the primacy of the judiciary, violating the basic structure

options.label: C
options.text: It failed to provide adequate representation for women and marginalized communities

options.label: D
options.text: The amendment procedure under Article 368 was not followed correctly

questions.solution: Correct answer: The inclusion of the Law Minister and two eminent persons impaired the primacy of the judiciary, violating the basic structure.

questions.text: Which case marked the beginning of the shift in locus standi by recognizing that a letter addressed to a judge could be treated as a writ petition?

options.label: A
options.text: Hussainara Khatoon v. State of Bihar (1979)

options.label: B
options.text: S.P. Gupta v. Union of India (1981)

options.label: C
options.text: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (1987)

options.label: D
options.text: Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India (1984)

questions.solution: Correct answer: S.P. Gupta v. Union of India (1981).

questions.text: Which of the following correctly matches the South African capital city with its governmental function?

options.label: A
options.text: Pretoria – Legislative; Cape Town – Executive; Bloemfontein – Judicial

options.label: B
options.text: Pretoria – Executive; Cape Town – Legislative; Bloemfontein – Judicial

options.label: C
options.text: Pretoria – Judicial; Cape Town – Executive; Bloemfontein – Legislative

options.label: D
options.text: Pretoria – Executive; Cape Town – Judicial; Bloemfontein – Legislative

questions.solution: Correct answer: Pretoria – Executive; Cape Town – Legislative; Bloemfontein – Judicial.

questions.text: Which group of countries was added to BRICS during its 2024 expansion?

options.label: A
options.text: Argentina, Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia

options.label: B
options.text: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE, Saudi Arabia

questions.solution: Correct answer: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE, Saudi Arabia.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the International Court of Justice (ICJ) from the International Criminal Court (ICC)?

options.label: A
options.text: ICJ prosecutes individuals for war crimes; ICC settles disputes between states.

options.label: B
options.text: ICJ settles disputes between states and gives advisory opinions; ICC prosecutes individuals for genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity, and aggression.

options.label: C
options.text: Both courts are principal organs of the United Nations and are seated in The Hague.

options.label: D
options.text: ICJ has 124 states parties; ICC has 15 judges elected for nine-year terms by the General Assembly and Security Council.

questions.solution: Correct answer: ICJ settles disputes between states and gives advisory opinions; ICC prosecutes individuals for genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity, and aggression..

questions.text: Which of the following describes a currency board arrangement as per the IMF's de‑jure classification?

options.label: A
options.text: The monetary authority holds foreign reserves equal to 100% of the monetary base, eliminating discretionary policy.

options.label: B
options.text: The domestic currency is replaced entirely by a foreign currency.

options.label: C
options.text: A fixed peg is maintained within a narrow band of ±1% against a single anchor.

options.label: D
options.text: The central bank intervenes without a published target in a managed float.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The monetary authority holds foreign reserves equal to 100% of the monetary base, eliminating discretionary policy..

questions.text: According to the IMF's COFER database (Q4 2023), which currency accounted for roughly 58% of allocated global reserves?
questions.solution: Correct answer: US dollar.

questions.text: Which body is responsible for selecting the Nobel Peace Prize laureate?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Norwegian Nobel Committee.

questions.text: What is the typical host arrangement for UN International Days?

options.label: B
options.text: Host rotates annually among member states

options.label: C
options.text: Host is always the UN headquarters in New York

options.label: D
options.text: Host is selected by the Secretary‑General for a five‑year term

questions.solution: Correct answer: Host rotates annually among member states.

questions.text: Which statement correctly distinguishes a Special Administrative Region (SAR) from a sovereign microstate?

options.label: A
options.text: SARs have full external sovereignty like microstates.

options.label: B
options.text: SARs lack external sovereignty but possess internal autonomy.

options.label: C
options.text: Microstates lack internal autonomy but have external sovereignty.

options.label: D
options.text: Both SARs and microstates are full UN members with identical rights.

questions.solution: Correct answer: SARs lack external sovereignty but possess internal autonomy..

questions.text: As of 2024, which of the following currencies is NOT included in the IMF's Special Drawing Rights (SDR) basket?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Swiss franc.

questions.text: Which treaty body monitors the implementation of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR)?

options.label: A
options.text: Committee on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (CESCR)

options.label: C
options.text: Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination (CERD)

questions.solution: Correct answer: Human Rights Committee (CCPR).

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a basis for the International Court of Justice (ICJ) to exercise contentious jurisdiction over a dispute between States?

options.label: A
options.text: A special agreement (compromis) between the parties

options.label: B
options.text: A compromissory clause in a treaty to which both States are parties

options.label: C
options.text: A unilateral declaration accepting the Court's compulsory jurisdiction under Article 36(2) of the ICJ Statute

options.label: D
options.text: A resolution of the UN General Assembly referring the dispute to the Court

questions.solution: Correct answer: A resolution of the UN General Assembly referring the dispute to the Court.

questions.text: What is the current status of the WTO Appellate Body and the interim arrangement adopted by some members?

options.label: A
options.text: The Appellate Body is fully functional with all seven members appointed.

options.label: B
options.text: The Appellate Body has been non-functional since December 2019, and the Multi-Party Interim Appeal Arbitration Arrangement (MPIA) serves as an interim appeal mechanism for participating members.

options.label: C
options.text: The Appellate Body was replaced permanently by the MPIA in 2020.

options.label: D
options.text: The Appellate Body is non-functional, but all WTO members are required to use the MPIA for appeals.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Appellate Body has been non-functional since December 2019, and the Multi-Party Interim Appeal Arbitration Arrangement (MPIA) serves as an interim appeal mechanism for participating members..

questions.text: How is the United States Congressional Gold Medal conferred?
questions.solution: Correct answer: By an act of Congress..

questions.text: Which body explicitly names the lead agency for a United Nations International Year?

options.label: B
options.text: The General Assembly through its resolution.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The General Assembly through its resolution..

questions.text: What is the typical practice of major international translation prizes regarding the distribution of prize money?

options.label: A
options.text: The prize is awarded solely to the translator.

options.label: B
options.text: The prize is split between the translator and the author, or both receive equal recognition.

options.label: C
options.text: The prize is awarded solely to the author.

options.label: D
options.text: The prize money is donated to a literary foundation.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The prize is split between the translator and the author, or both receive equal recognition..

questions.text: Which factor is a stronger indicator of a capital city's diplomatic hub status than the number of embassies?

options.label: B
options.text: Presence of permanent secretariats and recurring summit cycles.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Presence of permanent secretariats and recurring summit cycles..

questions.text: A principle paragraph in a CLAT item reads: "A person is liable for negligence if he owes a duty of care to the plaintiff, breaches that duty, and causes damage thereby, unless the plaintiff voluntarily assumed the risk." Which of the following correctly identifies the structural elements a candidate must underline while reading this principle?

options.label: A
options.text: Only the three positive conditions: duty of care, breach, and causation of damage.

options.label: B
options.text: The three positive conditions plus the qualifying phrase "unless the plaintiff voluntarily assumed the risk" as an exception.

options.label: C
options.text: The three positive conditions, but the "unless" clause is merely explanatory and not an operative exception.

options.label: D
options.text: The principle contains no exceptions because "unless" introduces a defence, not an element of the principle.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The three positive conditions plus the qualifying phrase "unless the plaintiff voluntarily assumed the risk" as an exception..

questions.text: A CLAT principle quotes Article 21 and adds: "No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law, and such procedure must be fair, just, and reasonable." The facts state the government impounded a citizen's passport without giving him a hearing or stating reasons. Which option correctly applies the principle?

options.label: A
options.text: The action is valid because Article 21 only protects life, not the right to hold a passport.

options.label: B
options.text: The action is invalid because the procedure lacked fairness, justice, and reasonableness by denying a hearing.

options.label: C
options.text: The action is valid because impounding a passport is an administrative act not subject to judicial review.

options.label: D
options.text: The action is invalid only if the citizen can prove the government acted with mala fide intent.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The action is invalid because the procedure lacked fairness, justice, and reasonableness by denying a hearing..

questions.text: In a principle-fact question, the principle requires "a voluntary act done with knowledge that it is likely to cause death." The facts show the accused pushed the victim during a sudden quarrel; the victim fell, hit his head, and died. The accused did not intend to kill. An answer option states: "The accused is liable because his act caused death." Which logical fallacy does this option exploit?

options.label: A
options.text: Denying the antecedent: it assumes that because the act was not intended to kill, it cannot be voluntary.

options.label: B
options.text: Affirming the consequent: it infers the presence of the required mental element (knowledge) solely from the occurrence of death.

options.label: C
options.text: Circular reasoning: it uses the conclusion (liability) as the premise for establishing the act was voluntary.

options.label: D
options.text: False dilemma: it presents only two extremes — either full liability or no liability — ignoring partial defences.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Affirming the consequent: it infers the presence of the required mental element (knowledge) solely from the occurrence of death..

questions.text: A state enacts a law that completely bans the sale of a certain chemical to protect public health. The government argues the ban pursues a legitimate aim and is rationally connected to that aim. However, a licensing regime with strict safety standards would achieve the same objective while imposing a lesser restriction on the right to trade. Under the four‑step proportionality test, at which step does the law fail?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Necessity.

questions.text: A delivery company employs a driver who, while delivering a parcel, assaults the recipient because of a personal grudge unrelated to the delivery. The company’s policy prohibits violence. Applying the “course of employment” test for vicarious liability, is the company liable?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, because the assault occurred during working hours and at the delivery location.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, because the risk of assault is inherent in the business of serving the public.

options.label: C
options.text: No, because the assault was a frolic — a personal act not a mode of performing the authorised task.

options.label: D
options.text: No, because the company had a policy prohibiting violence, which negates vicarious liability.

questions.solution: Correct answer: No, because the assault was a frolic — a personal act not a mode of performing the authorised task..

questions.text: The government issues a press release stating that it will provide a 20 % subsidy to manufacturers of solar panels. Relying on this announcement, a company invests ₹5 crore in a new production line. Before any formal notification or scheme is published, the government withdraws the announcement. The company claims a legitimate expectation. What factual element is essential for the claim to succeed?

options.label: A
options.text: The announcement must be made in a formal gazette notification.

options.label: B
options.text: The company must have suffered a detriment as a result of its reliance on the representation.

options.label: C
options.text: The government must have acted in bad faith when withdrawing the announcement.

options.label: D
options.text: The subsidy must be a statutory entitlement rather than a discretionary policy.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The company must have suffered a detriment as a result of its reliance on the representation..

questions.text: Parliament passes a constitutional amendment that removes the power of judicial review over all economic legislation, leaving only a limited appellate review. The amendment is challenged on the ground that it violates the basic structure of the Constitution. According to the basic structure doctrine as developed in Indian jurisprudence, what is the correct outcome?

options.label: A
options.text: The amendment is valid because Parliament’s plenary power under Article 368 permits any amendment.

options.label: B
options.text: The amendment is invalid because judicial review is a basic feature of the Constitution and cannot be removed even for a limited domain.

options.label: C
options.text: The amendment is valid because it only curtails judicial review in a specific policy area, not the entire power.

options.label: D
options.text: The amendment is invalid only if it also alters the identity of the Constitution’s preamble.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The amendment is invalid because judicial review is a basic feature of the Constitution and cannot be removed even for a limited domain..

questions.text: A chemical plant operates under a licence that permits emissions of a pollutant up to a specified limit. Due to a sudden equipment failure, the plant releases the pollutant at a level exceeding the licensed limit, damaging nearby crops. Under the Indian absolute liability principle laid down in M. C. Mehta v. Union of India, is the enterprise liable?

options.label: A
options.text: No, because the plant was operating under statutory authority, which is a complete defence.

options.label: B
options.text: No, because the escape occurred despite compliance with the licence conditions.

options.label: C
options.text: Yes, because absolute liability imposes responsibility irrespective of compliance with statutory limits and the licence does not authorise the escape.

options.label: D
options.text: Yes, but only if the claimant proves negligence in the maintenance of the equipment.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Yes, because absolute liability imposes responsibility irrespective of compliance with statutory limits and the licence does not authorise the escape..

questions.text: A State enacts the "Public Health (Regulation of Sale of Narcotic Substances) Act, 2023" prohibiting the retail sale of certain narcotic drugs within its territory. Entry 19 of the State List covers "public health and sanitation". Entry 56 of the Union List covers "regulation of narcotic drugs". The Act’s dominant purpose is to protect public health by restricting drug availability. Applying the doctrine of pith and substance, which conclusion follows?

options.label: A
options.text: The Act is ultra vires because it trenches on a Union List entry, and any overlap invalidates the law.

options.label: B
options.text: The Act is valid because its pith and substance is public health, a State subject, and incidental encroachment on the Union List is permissible.

options.label: C
options.text: The Act is valid only if the State obtains prior consent of the Union Parliament under Article 254.

options.label: D
options.text: The Act is void because the doctrine of pith and substance applies only to taxing statutes, not to regulatory legislation.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Act is valid because its pith and substance is public health, a State subject, and incidental encroachment on the Union List is permissible..

questions.text: A municipal commissioner issues an order cancelling a street‑vendor’s licence without giving the vendor any opportunity to be heard. The vendor challenges the order on the ground of violation of natural justice. The commissioner argues that the order is a purely administrative act and natural justice does not apply. Which principle correctly resolves the dispute?

options.label: A
options.text: Natural justice applies only to judicial functions; purely administrative decisions are exempt from any hearing requirement.

options.label: B
options.text: Natural justice applies to quasi‑judicial functions; cancellation of a licence is quasi‑judicial, so the vendor was entitled to a hearing.

options.label: C
options.text: Natural justice requires a full oral hearing in every administrative decision, regardless of its nature.

options.label: D
options.text: The vendor has no remedy because the commissioner enjoys absolute discretion in licensing matters.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Natural justice applies to quasi‑judicial functions; cancellation of a licence is quasi‑judicial, so the vendor was entitled to a hearing..

questions.text: The Supreme Court issues a mandatory direction to the State Government to implement a mid‑day meal scheme in all government schools within six months, citing the fundamental right to nutrition under Article 21. A principle states: "Judicial activism is characterised by courts directing policy implementation and creating new norms where the legislature has been inactive." How would the Court’s direction be classified under this principle?

options.label: A
options.text: Judicial restraint, because the Court merely enforced an existing statutory obligation.

options.label: B
options.text: Judicial activism, because the Court directed policy implementation in the absence of legislation.

options.label: C
options.text: Neither activism nor restraint, because the direction was based on a fundamental right.

options.label: D
options.text: Judicial restraint, because the Court deferred to the executive’s policy expertise.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Judicial activism, because the Court directed policy implementation in the absence of legislation..

questions.text: An environmental authority refuses to renew a factory’s pollution‑control consent, citing "unreasonable" emissions data. The factory challenges the refusal in the High Court, arguing the decision is Wednesbury‑unreasonable. The Court applies the Wednesbury test. Which statement accurately reflects the standard of review?

options.label: A
options.text: The Court will substitute its own view of the emissions data and decide whether the refusal was correct on merits.

options.label: B
options.text: The Court will interfere only if the decision is so unreasonable that no reasonable authority could have reached it.

options.label: C
options.text: The Court will apply a proportionality test, balancing the factory’s economic interest against environmental protection.

options.label: D
options.text: The Court will treat any error of law in interpreting the emissions standards as Wednesbury unreasonableness.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Court will interfere only if the decision is so unreasonable that no reasonable authority could have reached it..

questions.text: Section 5 of the Commercial Contracts Act provides: "All contracts for the sale of goods shall be in writing." Section 12 of the same Act states: "Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, oral agreements for the sale of goods valued below five hundred rupees shall be enforceable." A dispute arises over an oral agreement for goods worth four hundred rupees. Which interpretive principle resolves the apparent conflict?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Doctrine of Harmonious Construction.

questions.text: The Environmental Protection Act contains ten independent sections. Section 4, which empowers the Central Government to set emission standards for a specific industry, is declared unconstitutional for violating Article 19(1)(g). The remaining nine sections regulate unrelated matters and can operate without Section 4. Which doctrine permits the rest of the Act to survive?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Doctrine of Severability.

questions.text: The Supreme Court declares a regulatory regime governing telecom licences unconstitutional but expressly states that all licences already granted under the regime shall remain valid until their expiry. The Court invokes a doctrine that limits the effect of its declaration to future cases. Which doctrine is being applied?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Doctrine of Prospective Overruling.

questions.text: 'Audi alteram partem' means:

options.label: B
options.text: No one should judge their own case

options.label: C
options.text: Ignorance of law is no excuse

questions.solution: Correct answer: Hear the other side.

questions.text: 'Nemo judex in causa sua' means:

options.label: A
options.text: No one should be a judge in their own case

options.label: C
options.text: Ignorance of law is no excuse

options.label: D
options.text: To a willing person, no injury

questions.solution: Correct answer: No one should be a judge in their own case.

questions.text: Damnum sine injuria means:

options.label: A
options.text: Damage without legal injury — not actionable

questions.solution: Correct answer: Damage without legal injury — not actionable.

questions.text: Injuria sine damno means:
questions.solution: Correct answer: Legal injury without damage — actionable.

questions.text: 'Res ipsa loquitur' means:
questions.solution: Correct answer: The thing speaks for itself.

questions.text: A constitutional amendment is challenged on the ground that it destroys the federal character of the Constitution by converting States into mere administrative units. The Supreme Court strikes down the amendment. Which maxim correctly captures the legal consequence and the doctrinal basis for this outcome?

options.label: A
options.text: The amendment is voidable under the doctrine of eclipse, as it is inconsistent with fundamental rights.

options.label: B
options.text: The amendment is void ab initio under the basic structure doctrine, as it violates constitutional supremacy.

options.label: C
options.text: The amendment is ultra vires the legislative competence of Parliament under Article 368.

options.label: D
options.text: The amendment is intra vires but inoperative under the principle of severability until the federal structure is restored.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The amendment is void ab initio under the basic structure doctrine, as it violates constitutional supremacy..

questions.text: The Government announces a policy to regularize all ad-hoc employees with 10 years of service. Relying on this, an employee declines a private job offer. Before regularization, the Government withdraws the policy citing fiscal constraints, without hearing the employee. The employee challenges the withdrawal. Which principle governs the outcome?

options.label: A
options.text: The employee has a substantive right to regularization because the policy created a legitimate expectation enforceable as a contract.

options.label: B
options.text: The withdrawal is valid because legitimate expectation is merely a moral claim with no legal enforceability against the State.

options.label: C
options.text: The withdrawal is invalid because legitimate expectation requires a hearing before frustration, unless overriding public interest is shown, which mere fiscal constraints may not satisfy.

options.label: D
options.text: The employee can claim damages for breach of promise under promissory estoppel, but cannot compel regularization.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The withdrawal is invalid because legitimate expectation requires a hearing before frustration, unless overriding public interest is shown, which mere fiscal constraints may not satisfy..

questions.text: A State Legislature enacts a law imposing a tax on "services rendered by way of legal consultation". The State argues it falls under Entry 62 (taxes on professions) of the State List. The Union argues it encroaches on Entry 97 (residuary power) or constitutes a tax on services (GST domain). The Court finds the true nature of the levy is a tax on the profession of advocates. Which maxim resolves this competence dispute?

options.label: A
options.text: Colourable legislation — the State has misused its power by labelling a service tax as a profession tax.

options.label: B
options.text: Pith and substance — the true character of the legislation determines its legislative competence.

options.label: C
options.text: Ultra vires — the State lacks any power to tax legal services under the Seventh Schedule.

options.label: D
options.text: Basic structure — federalism is violated if States tax professional services exclusively regulated by the Bar Council.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Pith and substance — the true character of the legislation determines its legislative competence..

questions.text: A consumer purchases a sealed, branded pressure cooker from a retailer. While using it according to instructions, the cooker explodes due to a manufacturing defect, causing injury. The retailer argues the consumer failed to inspect the cooker before use. In a claim under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, which maxim is most directly applicable to establish the retailer's liability?

options.label: A
options.text: Caveat emptor — the buyer had a duty to inspect the goods before use.

options.label: B
options.text: Res ipsa loquitur — the explosion implies negligence by the manufacturer/retailer who had control.

options.label: C
options.text: Uberrima fides — the retailer failed to disclose the latent defect known to them.

options.label: D
options.text: Caveat venditor — statutory strict liability attaches to the seller for defective products.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Caveat venditor — statutory strict liability attaches to the seller for defective products..

questions.text: A fires a pistol at B intending to kill him. The bullet misses B but strikes and kills C, a bystander standing behind B. A is charged with the murder of C. Which statement correctly applies the doctrine of transferred malice and the coincidence principle?

options.label: A
options.text: A is liable for murder of C because the mens rea (intention to kill) directed at B transfers to C, satisfying the coincidence of actus reus and mens rea.

options.label: B
options.text: A is liable only for attempt to murder B and culpable homicide for C, as the actus reus (killing C) differs from the intended actus reus (killing B).

options.label: C
options.text: A is not liable for murder of C because the doctrine of transferred malice applies only if the intended victim and actual victim are in the same legal category.

options.label: D
