options.text: A is liable for murder of C under strict liability, as the act of firing a gun in public creates absolute liability for any resulting death.

questions.solution: Correct answer: A is liable for murder of C because the mens rea (intention to kill) directed at B transfers to C, satisfying the coincidence of actus reus and mens rea..

questions.text: A five-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court decides a question of constitutional interpretation. Two years later, a three-judge Bench of the same Court, unaware of a relevant constitutional amendment enacted after the Constitution Bench decision, renders a judgment contradicting the earlier ruling. A High Court is seized of a case involving the same constitutional question. Which precedent is the High Court bound to follow?

options.label: A
options.text: The three-judge Bench decision, as it is the most recent pronouncement of the Supreme Court.

options.label: B
options.text: The Constitution Bench decision, because the later judgment was rendered per incuriam and carries no precedential weight.

options.label: C
options.text: Neither, as the High Court must refer the matter to a larger Bench of the Supreme Court under Article 143.

options.label: D
options.text: The three-judge Bench decision, because a smaller Bench can overrule a larger Bench if it identifies an error in reasoning.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Constitution Bench decision, because the later judgment was rendered per incuriam and carries no precedential weight..

questions.text: A plaintiff seeks specific performance of a contract to purchase agricultural land. The defendant pleads that the plaintiff, while negotiating, fraudulently concealed that the land was notified for compulsory acquisition by the government. The plaintiff argues that the defendant's remedy lies in damages, not in denying equitable relief. The court finds the plaintiff's concealment proven. Which equitable maxim bars the plaintiff's claim?

options.label: A
options.text: Delay defeats equity, because the plaintiff delayed filing the suit after learning of the acquisition notification.

options.label: B
options.text: Equity follows the law, because the Land Acquisition Act provides a statutory remedy that overrides equitable relief.

options.label: C
options.text: He who comes into equity must come with clean hands, because the plaintiff's fraudulent concealment disentitles him to equitable relief.

options.label: D
options.text: He who seeks equity must do equity, because the plaintiff must compensate the defendant for the loss caused by the acquisition.

questions.solution: Correct answer: He who comes into equity must come with clean hands, because the plaintiff's fraudulent concealment disentitles him to equitable relief..

questions.text: State X and State Y are parties to a bilateral treaty permitting the use of certain chemical agents in riot control. Subsequently, the UN General Assembly adopts a resolution declaring the prohibition of such chemical agents a peremptory norm of general international law (jus cogens). State X invokes the treaty to justify using the agents against protesters. State Y protests, arguing the treaty is void. Which principle determines the treaty's validity?

options.label: A
options.text: Pacta sunt servanda, because the treaty was validly concluded and remains binding until formally terminated by either party.

options.label: B
options.text: Jus cogens, because a treaty conflicting with a peremptory norm is void under Article 53 of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties.

options.label: C
options.text: Erga omnes, because the prohibition creates obligations owed to the international community as a whole, allowing any state to challenge the treaty.

options.label: D
options.text: Rebus sic stantibus, because the fundamental change in international law permits termination of the treaty due to changed circumstances.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Jus cogens, because a treaty conflicting with a peremptory norm is void under Article 53 of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties..

questions.text: A witness in a criminal trial is proven to have deliberately lied about a material fact during cross-examination. The defence counsel argues that under the maxim falsus in uno falsus in omnibus, the court must reject the witness's entire testimony. How should the court proceed?

options.label: A
options.text: Reject the entire testimony as the maxim is a mandatory rule of evidence

options.label: B
options.text: Disregard only the false portion and accept the remainder if independently credible

options.label: C
options.text: Evaluate the remaining testimony separately, considering whether the falsehood goes to the root of credibility

options.label: D
options.text: Accept the testimony in full because the maxim has been abolished in Indian law

questions.solution: Correct answer: Evaluate the remaining testimony separately, considering whether the falsehood goes to the root of credibility.

questions.text: A thief steals a car and sells it to a bona fide purchaser for value without notice of the theft. The purchaser claims title against the true owner, arguing that the 'market overt' doctrine or a general bona fide purchaser exception protects him. Under Indian law, what is the outcome?

options.label: A
options.text: The purchaser acquires good title under the market overt doctrine

options.label: B
options.text: The purchaser acquires good title under the general bona fide purchaser exception

options.label: C
options.text: The purchaser does not acquire title because nemo dat quod non habet applies and exceptions are strictly statutory

options.label: D
options.text: The true owner is estopped from denying the seller's authority because he left the car unattended

questions.solution: Correct answer: The purchaser does not acquire title because nemo dat quod non habet applies and exceptions are strictly statutory.

questions.text: The directors of a company enter into a contract on behalf of the company. The contract is within the objects clause of the Memorandum of Association but exceeds the directors' authority under the Articles of Association. The company seeks to avoid the contract. What is the legal position?

options.label: A
options.text: The contract is void ab initio as ultra vires the company

options.label: B
options.text: The contract is voidable at the instance of the company

options.label: C
options.text: The contract is voidable at the instance of the third party

options.label: D
options.text: The contract is irregular but curable by shareholder ratification

questions.solution: Correct answer: The contract is irregular but curable by shareholder ratification.

questions.text: A plaintiff files a suit for defamation against the defendant. During the pendency of the suit, the plaintiff dies. The plaintiff's legal representatives apply to be substituted and continue the suit. The defendant objects, citing the maxim actio personalis moritur cum persona. How should the court decide?

options.label: A
options.text: Allow substitution because defamation is a tort and all tort claims survive

options.label: B
options.text: Allow substitution only if the defamation caused pecuniary loss to the plaintiff's estate

options.label: C
options.text: Reject substitution because personal actions for defamation abate on death

options.label: D
options.text: Reject substitution but allow a fresh suit by the legal representatives for injury to reputation

questions.solution: Correct answer: Reject substitution because personal actions for defamation abate on death.

questions.text: Under the principle 'Whoever causes death by a rash or negligent act is guilty', a driver driving carefully who hits a child who suddenly darted onto the road is:
questions.solution: Correct answer: Not guilty.

questions.text: Which principle applies when a person knowingly assumes a risk?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Volenti non fit injuria.

questions.text: Which is NOT an essential of negligence in tort?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Malicious intention.

questions.text: Article 21 of the Constitution guarantees:

options.label: B
options.text: Right to life and personal liberty

questions.solution: Correct answer: Right to life and personal liberty.

questions.text: In a contract, 'consideration' means:
questions.solution: Correct answer: Something of value exchanged.

questions.text: An employee of a courier company, while delivering a package, detours 15 kilometres to visit a friend and causes an accident. The employer argues the employee was on a "frolic of his own". Which factor is decisive for determining whether the employer remains vicariously liable?

options.label: A
options.text: Whether the employer exercised direct control over the manner of driving at the time of the accident

options.label: B
options.text: Whether the act of driving was expressly authorised by the employer

options.label: C
options.text: The degree of deviation from the assigned delivery route and duties

options.label: D
options.text: The employee's personal motive for making the detour

questions.solution: Correct answer: The degree of deviation from the assigned delivery route and duties.

questions.text: Under Section 56 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, a contract is frustrated when a supervening event makes performance impossible or unlawful. Which of the following is NOT a required element for frustration?

options.label: A
options.text: The event occurs without fault of either party

options.label: B
options.text: The event was unforeseen and not provided for in the contract

options.label: C
options.text: The event renders performance merely more expensive or delayed

options.label: D
options.text: The event destroys the foundation of the contract or makes performance fundamentally different

questions.solution: Correct answer: The event renders performance merely more expensive or delayed.

questions.text: In criminal law, the presumption regarding mens rea for regulatory offences is best described by which statement?

options.label: A
options.text: All regulatory offences are strict liability offences by default

options.label: B
options.text: Courts presume mens rea unless the statute expressly excludes it, especially when imprisonment is prescribed

options.label: C
options.text: Specific intent must be proved for every regulatory offence

options.label: D
options.text: General intent is sufficient to convict for any strict liability offence

questions.solution: Correct answer: Courts presume mens rea unless the statute expressly excludes it, especially when imprisonment is prescribed.

questions.text: Under Hindu law, which statement accurately reflects the position on matrimonial property division on divorce?

options.label: A
options.text: The wife automatically receives half of the husband’s property upon divorce

options.label: B
options.text: There is no automatic community of property; division depends on joint ownership and judicial discretion

options.label: C
options.text: The Hindu Succession Act, 2005 grants the wife an equal share in all of the husband’s self‑acquired property

options.label: D
options.text: Section 27 of the Hindu Marriage Act allows division of all property acquired during the marriage regardless of title

questions.solution: Correct answer: There is no automatic community of property; division depends on joint ownership and judicial discretion.

questions.text: A chemical plant licensed under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 stores large quantities of toxic gas. An unprecedented earthquake — an act of God — causes a tank rupture, releasing gas that kills nearby residents. The plant management pleads the defence of act of God and statutory compliance. Under the principle of absolute liability established in M.C. Mehta v. Union of India, what is the plant's liability?

options.label: A
options.text: The plant is not liable because the escape was caused by an unforeseeable act of God, which is a valid defence under absolute liability.

options.label: B
options.text: The plant is absolutely liable because hazardous industries owe a non-delegable duty to the community, and no defence of act of God, statutory authority, or due care is available.

options.label: C
options.text: The plant is liable only under the rule in Rylands v Fletcher if the residents prove negligence in maintenance of the tanks.

options.label: D
options.text: The plant is not liable because the statutory licence under the Environment (Protection) Act expressly authorizes the activity and compliance shields the enterprise.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The plant is absolutely liable because hazardous industries owe a non-delegable duty to the community, and no defence of act of God, statutory authority, or due care is available..

questions.text: A purchases poison, mixes it into a dish of food, and places the dish on the dining table where B usually eats dinner. A intends to kill B. Before B returns home, the police, acting on a tip-off, enter the house and seize the dish. A is charged with attempt to murder under Section 307 IPC read with Section 511 IPC. Applying the proximity test from Mohd. Yakub v. State, what is the correct legal position?

options.label: A
options.text: A is guilty of attempt because he completed all preparatory steps and the act of placing the poisoned food is proximate to the commission of murder.

options.label: B
options.text: A is guilty of attempt because mixing poison and placing the food constitutes an act towards the commission of the offence under Section 511 IPC.

options.label: C
options.text: A is not guilty of attempt; the acts amount only to preparation because B was not present and the chain of causation could still be broken by A's voluntary desistance or external intervention.

options.label: D
options.text: A is not guilty of attempt because the poison was not actually consumed, and attempt requires the last act necessary for completion of the offence.

questions.solution: Correct answer: A is not guilty of attempt; the acts amount only to preparation because B was not present and the chain of causation could still be broken by A's voluntary desistance or external intervention..

questions.text: A State Government issues a notification announcing a new recruitment policy for Group C posts, stating that candidates who have cleared a specific skill test will be given preference. Relying on this, 500 candidates appear for and clear the test. Before appointments are made, the Government withdraws the notification without giving the candidates a hearing. The candidates challenge the withdrawal. Applying the doctrine of legitimate expectation, which conclusion follows?

options.label: A
options.text: The candidates have a substantive legitimate expectation to appointment because they fulfilled the condition in the notification.

options.label: B
options.text: The candidates have a procedural legitimate expectation to be heard before the policy is withdrawn, as the notification created a clear representation.

options.label: C
options.text: The candidates have no legitimate expectation because recruitment is a sovereign function and promissory estoppel does not apply against the State.

options.label: D
options.text: The candidates can claim a substantive right to appointment under Article 14, as the withdrawal is manifestly arbitrary.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The candidates have a procedural legitimate expectation to be heard before the policy is withdrawn, as the notification created a clear representation..

questions.text: Which of the following numbers is an integer but not a whole number?
questions.solution: Correct answer: -3.

questions.text: Which of the following four‑digit numbers is divisible by 11 according to the divisibility rule?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 3080.

questions.text: Evaluate the expression: 12 + 18 ÷ 3 × (4 - 1)² - 5.
questions.solution: Correct answer: 61.

questions.text: How many integers from 1 to 500 inclusive are divisible by at least one of 3, 5, or 7?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 271.

questions.text: What is the sum of all positive integers k ≤ 360 such that gcd(k, 360) = 1?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 17280.

questions.text: Denest the radical √(11 − 6√2).
questions.solution: Correct answer: 3 − √2.

questions.text: Let X be the face value of a fair die roll. If Var(X) = 35/12, what is Var(2X + 3)?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 35/3.

questions.text: The probability of a defective item is 0.02. In a sample of 100 items, approximate the probability of at most 3 defectives using the Poisson distribution.
questions.solution: Correct answer: 0.857.

questions.text: Compute φ(720) using the product formula for Euler's totient function.
questions.solution: Correct answer: 192.

questions.text: Simplify the nested radical √(7+4√3).
questions.solution: Correct answer: 2+√3.

questions.text: How many derangements (permutations with no fixed points) exist for 5 distinct objects?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 44.

questions.text: How many solutions does the congruence x^2 ≡ 3 (mod 13) have?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 2.

questions.text: For which of the following moduli does a primitive root NOT exist?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 8.

questions.text: What is the number of onto functions from a 5‑element set to a 3‑element set?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 150.

questions.text: A factory produces 20 000 items per day with a defect rate of 0.0005. Which approximation is most appropriate for the probability of at most 8 defects in a day?

options.label: D
options.text: Both Poisson and normal approximations are equally accurate

questions.solution: Correct answer: Poisson approximation with λ = 10.

questions.text: A spherical cap of height 3 is cut from a sphere of radius 5. What is the volume of the cap?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 36π.

questions.text: If a company's revenue rose from ₹400 crore to ₹500 crore, the percentage increase is:
questions.solution: Correct answer: 25%.

questions.text: In a pie chart, 25% corresponds to an angle of:
questions.solution: Correct answer: 90°.

questions.text: If A:B = 2:3 and B:C = 4:5, then A:C =
questions.solution: Correct answer: 8:15.

questions.text: 1/8 as a percentage is:
questions.solution: Correct answer: 12.5%.

questions.text: Data interpretation answers must be based on:
questions.solution: Correct answer: The given data only.

questions.text: Two time series are recorded for five consecutive years. Series A (₹ crore): 100, 120, 150, 180, 210 Series B (million units): 50, 55, 65, 70, 80 In how many years does the year‑on‑year growth rate of Series A exceed that of Series B?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 4.

questions.text: CP = ₹200, SP = ₹250. Profit% is:
questions.solution: Correct answer: 25%.

questions.text: Tea at ₹60/kg and ₹90/kg mixed to get ₹75/kg. Ratio (cheaper:dearer):
questions.solution: Correct answer: 1:1.

questions.text: A completes work in 10 days, B in 15 days. Together:
questions.solution: Correct answer: 6 days.

questions.text: SI on ₹1000 at 10% for 2 years:
questions.solution: Correct answer: ₹200.

questions.text: If A:B = 2:3 and B:C = 4:5, A:C =
questions.solution: Correct answer: 8:15.

questions.text: What comes next in the number series: 3, 6, 12, 24, ?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 48.

questions.text: Identify the Odd One Out from the following set: A) Apple B) Banana C) Carrot D) Grape
questions.solution: Correct answer: C.

questions.text: Complete the letter series: Z, Y, X, W, ?
questions.solution: Correct answer: V.

questions.text: Keyboard : Input :: Monitor : Output :: Processor : ?
questions.solution: Correct answer: CPU.

questions.text: If a number is even it must be a multiple of 4; otherwise it must be prime. Which number violates this rule?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 9.

questions.text: In the series 3, 6, 12, 24, ?, which time‑pressure heuristic yields the answer fastest?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Two‑Term Lock.

questions.text: In the recursive analogy ‘Pseudo‑science : Science :: Pseudo‑scientific : ?’, the prefix ‘pseudo‑’ forms a noun in the first pair and an adjective in the second. Applying the same morphological operator to the base term yields which answer?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Scientific.

questions.text: The analogy ‘Adult : Child :: Kitten : ?’ exhibits a relational reversal: the first pair orders the terms as ‘older : younger’, while the second pair requires the reverse order ‘younger : older’. Which option correctly completes the analogy?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Cat.

questions.text: In the set {Oak, Pine, Maple, Spruce, Fern}, four members belong to the taxonomic group of seed‑producing trees (gymnosperms or angiosperms), while one is a non‑seed vascular plant. At the deepest scientific classification level, which item is the odd one out?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Fern.

questions.text: Algorithm : Subroutine :: Program : ?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Function.

questions.text: Recipe : Ingredients :: Algorithm : ?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Data.

questions.text: Select the word that does not belong: Lion, Tiger, Leopard, Cheetah, Panther.
questions.solution: Correct answer: Cheetah.

questions.text: A sequence is defined by a₁ = 5 and aₙ = 2·aₙ₋₁ − n for n ≥ 2. What is the 4th term?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 22.

questions.text: In the triple analogy Mammal : Dog :: Bird : Sparrow :: Reptile : ?, which option completes the third mapping while preserving the same class‑to‑prototypical‑instance relation at all three levels?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Lizard.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs exhibits the identical relational verb phrase "instrument used by the primary practitioner of" as the stem pair Scalpel : Surgeon?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Pen : Author.

questions.text: The sequence 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, … follows the triangular number formula Tₙ = n(n+1)/2. What is the 8th term of this series?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 36.

questions.text: A modular arithmetic series is given as 5, 11, 4, 10, 3, 9, … . Assuming the rule "add a constant k modulo m" generates the series, what is the modulus m?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 13.

questions.text: In the analogy "cell : nucleus :: computer : CPU :: organization : headquarters", which relational schema must the correct answer preserve?
questions.solution: Correct answer: system : central control unit.

questions.text: Five items are described by four attributes (shape, colour, size, material): 1. (circle, red, small, plastic) 2. (circle, red, small, metal) 3. (circle, blue, small, plastic) 4. (square, red, small, plastic) 5. (circle, red, large, plastic) Using the majority-profile method with Hamming distance, which item is the odd one out?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Item 2.

questions.text: A piecewise series starts at 2. Rule: if current term < 20, multiply by 3; otherwise subtract 7. What is the 8th term?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 19.

questions.text: An argument claims: "Since the new policy reduces traffic congestion, it will improve air quality." Which of the following is a necessary assumption for this argument?

options.label: A
options.text: Reducing traffic congestion leads to improved air quality.

options.label: B
options.text: The new policy will be popular among commuters.

options.label: C
options.text: Air quality is the only factor affected by traffic congestion.

options.label: D
options.text: The policy will be implemented without delay.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Reducing traffic congestion leads to improved air quality..

questions.text: The argument: "A new teaching method improves test scores because it increases student engagement." Which option would most strengthen this argument?

options.label: A
options.text: A study showing higher engagement scores in classrooms using the method.

options.label: B
options.text: The method is cheaper than traditional methods.

options.label: C
options.text: The author of the method is a well‑known educator.

options.label: D
options.text: The method has been adopted in several other countries.

questions.solution: Correct answer: A study showing higher engagement scores in classrooms using the method..

questions.text: An argument observes that ice‑cream sales rise when drowning incidents rise and concludes that ice‑cream consumption causes drowning. Which logical flaw does this argument exhibit?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Correlation versus causation.

questions.text: Given the conditional statement "If it rains, then the ground gets wet," which of the following conclusions is logically valid?

options.label: A
options.text: If the ground is not wet, then it did not rain.

options.label: B
options.text: If the ground is wet, then it rained.

options.label: C
options.text: If it did not rain, then the ground is not wet.

options.label: D
options.text: If it rained, then the ground is not wet.

questions.solution: Correct answer: If the ground is not wet, then it did not rain..

questions.text: In argument mapping, a box that has no incoming arrows and is not the main conclusion indicates which of the following?
questions.solution: Correct answer: A hidden premise.

questions.text: Given the conditional chain “If A then B; if B then C; if C then D,” which inference is logically valid without assuming biconditionals?
questions.solution: Correct answer: ¬D → ¬A.

questions.text: When evaluating an analogical argument, which critical question must be asked to test its strength?

options.label: B
options.text: Do the shared properties bear on the inferred property?

options.label: C
options.text: Is the analogy presented by an authority?

options.label: D
options.text: Does the analogy use emotional language?

questions.solution: Correct answer: Do the shared properties bear on the inferred property?.

questions.text: The argument “Because the new law reduces traffic fatalities, it should be adopted nationwide” relies on a hidden premise. What is that premise?

options.label: A
options.text: The law is popular among voters

options.label: B
options.text: Local conditions (road design, enforcement culture) are replicable elsewhere

options.label: C
options.text: The law has no unintended side effects

questions.solution: Correct answer: Local conditions (road design, enforcement culture) are replicable elsewhere.

questions.text: A universal claim “All policies that increase taxes reduce economic growth” can be refuted by which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: A statistical trend showing growth after a tax increase

options.label: B
options.text: A single historical case where a tax increase coincided with growth

options.label: C
options.text: An expert opinion that tax increases sometimes help

questions.solution: Correct answer: A single historical case where a tax increase coincided with growth.

questions.text: A policy brief argues: "Since 85% of surveyed economists support carbon pricing, the government should implement a carbon tax immediately." The brief treats the survey as conclusive proof without addressing whether the sample represents the relevant specialist sub-field or whether dissenting views exist. In Toulmin terms, which component is most directly flawed by this omission?

options.label: A
options.text: The claim, because it asserts a policy prescription rather than a factual conclusion

options.label: B
options.text: The data, because the survey percentage is factually incorrect

options.label: C
options.text: The warrant, because the inferential bridge from expert survey to policy necessity assumes consensus and representativeness without backing

options.label: D
options.text: The qualifier, because the argument uses "should" instead of "probably should"

questions.solution: Correct answer: The warrant, because the inferential bridge from expert survey to policy necessity assumes consensus and representativeness without backing.

questions.text: An editorial argues: "Professor Chen, a distinguished physicist, testified that the new nuclear waste storage facility poses no significant geological risk. Therefore, the facility is safe." Which critical question from Walton's expert opinion scheme most directly challenges the argument's validity?

options.label: A
options.text: Is Professor Chen's testimony biased by research funding from the nuclear industry?

options.label: B
options.text: Is there consensus among geologists and seismologists on the facility's geological risk?

options.label: C
options.text: Has Professor Chen published peer-reviewed papers on nuclear waste storage?

options.label: D
options.text: Does the argument acknowledge the possibility of human error in facility operation?

questions.solution: Correct answer: Is there consensus among geologists and seismologists on the facility's geological risk?.

questions.text: A study claims: "Cities with higher police funding have higher crime rates; therefore, increased police funding causes higher crime." The study aggregates data across all cities without controlling for city size, poverty rates, or pre-existing crime trends. Which statistical flaw does this argument most clearly exhibit?

options.label: A
options.text: Base-rate neglect, because the argument ignores the overall probability of crime in the population

options.label: B
options.text: Simpson's paradox, because the aggregated trend reverses when data are disaggregated by confounding variables like city size

options.label: C
options.text: Post hoc ergo propter hoc, because the argument infers causation from temporal sequence alone

options.label: D
options.text: Sampling bias, because the cities studied were not randomly selected from all cities

questions.solution: Correct answer: Simpson's paradox, because the aggregated trend reverses when data are disaggregated by confounding variables like city size.

questions.text: A researcher observes that the laboratory lights are off and concludes that the main power station has failed. Which of the following would most strengthen this abductive inference?

options.label: A
options.text: A controlled experiment shows that power‑station failures cause building‑wide outages in 95% of cases.

options.label: B
options.text: A local fuse blow is discovered that also explains the lights being off.

options.label: C
options.text: The researcher asserts that no other cause could possibly produce the observed effect.

options.label: D
options.text: The base‑rate probability of power‑station failure in the region is extremely low.

questions.solution: Correct answer: A controlled experiment shows that power‑station failures cause building‑wide outages in 95% of cases..

questions.text: In Chisholm’s contrary‑to‑duty paradox, standard deontic logic struggles because it cannot represent which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: Conditional obligations that trigger only when a primary obligation is violated.

options.label: B
options.text: The interdefinability of permission and obligation operators.

options.label: C
options.text: The consistency of multiple simultaneous obligations.

options.label: D
options.text: The derivation of a deontic conclusion from a factual premise.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Conditional obligations that trigger only when a primary obligation is violated..

questions.text: According to the Prakken & Sartor dialogue‑game model, a premise counts as “granted” in a critical discussion only if:

options.label: A
options.text: It belongs to the shared commitment base of the participants.

options.label: B
options.text: It is asserted by the proponent without challenge.

options.label: C
options.text: The opponent explicitly concedes it in the current move.

options.label: D
options.text: It is supported by an external authority cited in the dialogue.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It belongs to the shared commitment base of the participants..

questions.text: Consider an abstract argumentation framework with arguments A, B, C, D and attacks: A attacks B, B attacks C, C attacks A, and D is unattacked. Under grounded semantics, which argument(s) must be accepted (i.e., are skeptically justified)?
questions.solution: Correct answer: D only.

questions.text: Which of the following errors is committed when an argument treats an abductive conclusion as if it were deductively certain?

options.label: A
options.text: Ignoring rival explanations that could also account for the evidence.

options.label: B
options.text: Applying Occam’s razor when competing explanations have unequal explanatory power.

options.label: C
options.text: Confusing the base‑rate probability of the hypothesis with its posterior probability.

options.label: D
options.text: Concluding that the explanation is true because it is the simplest.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Ignoring rival explanations that could also account for the evidence..

questions.text: Premise: All managers are leaders. Which of the following conclusions follows necessarily?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Some leaders are managers.

questions.text: Premises: (1) All poets are dreamers. (2) Some dreamers are writers. Which conclusion follows?
questions.solution: Correct answer: No conclusion follows.

questions.text: Premises: (1) No cats are dogs. (2) Some dogs are pets. Which conclusion is valid?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Some pets are not cats.

questions.text: Premises: (1) All A are B. (2) Some B are not C. Consider the two conclusions: (i) Some A are not C. (ii) No A are C. Which statement about these conclusions is correct?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Neither conclusion follows.

questions.text: Premises: (1) No engineers are artists. (2) Some artists are musicians. Which conclusion can be validly drawn?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Some musicians are not engineers.

questions.text: Under the Boolean interpretation of categorical syllogisms, why is the mood Darapti (AAI‑3) invalid?

options.label: A
options.text: The middle term is not distributed in either premise.

options.label: B
options.text: The premises are both universal while the conclusion is particular, asserting existence not guaranteed.

options.label: C
options.text: The singular subject lacks existential import.

options.label: D
options.text: The conclusion illicitly distributes the minor term.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The premises are both universal while the conclusion is particular, asserting existence not guaranteed..

questions.text: A relational syllogism states: ‘All A are related to B by R; all B are related to C by R; therefore all A are related to C by R.’ This inference is valid only when the relation R possesses which property?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Transitivity.

questions.text: In a disjunctive syllogism using an inclusive ‘or’, the argument ‘P or Q; P; therefore not Q’ exemplifies which formal fallacy?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Affirming a disjunct.

questions.text: When a categorical syllogism is rendered into natural deduction, a particular conclusion (∃x) can be derived only if the premise set includes at least one:
questions.solution: Correct answer: Existential premise.

questions.text: Treating a singular statement such as ‘Socrates is mortal’ as a mere universal affirmative without acknowledging that its subject class is non‑empty commits which logical error?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Existential fallacy.

questions.text: Consider the following premises: 1. All engineers are technicians. 2. Some technicians are managers. The term "technicians" is used in the first premise to denote a professional qualification and in the second premise to denote a functional role. Which of the following correctly describes the logical status of the argument?

options.label: C
options.text: Either some engineers are managers or no engineers are managers.

questions.solution: Correct answer: No conclusion follows..

questions.text: Premises: 1. All scientists respect some philosophers. 2. All philosophers respect some artists. Which conclusion, if any, follows validly from these premises?
questions.solution: Correct answer: No conclusion follows..

questions.text: Under the modern Boolean interpretation (no existential import unless explicitly stated), which immediate inference from the proposition "All A are B" is valid?
questions.solution: Correct answer: No A are non‑B..

questions.text: Premise: "If the contract is signed, then the project will start." Fact: "The project has started." Which conclusion is logically justified?

options.label: C
options.text: The contract may or may not have been signed.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The contract may or may not have been signed..

questions.text: Premise: "Either the meeting is on Monday or it is on Tuesday." Fact: "The meeting is not on Monday." Assuming the disjunction is inclusive unless exclusivity is stated, which conclusion follows?

options.label: B
options.text: The meeting is not on Tuesday.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The meeting is on Tuesday..

questions.text: Under the Boolean (no‑existential‑import) interpretation adopted by most contemporary logical‑reasoning tests, does the conclusion “Some unicorns are white” follow from the single premise “All unicorns are white”?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, it follows because the universal affirms the particular.

options.label: B
options.text: No, it does not follow unless an explicit existential premise is added.

options.label: C
options.text: Yes, it follows only if the test‑maker states “Assume existential import”.

options.label: D
options.text: No, it follows only when the subject class is known to be non‑empty.

questions.solution: Correct answer: No, it does not follow unless an explicit existential premise is added..

questions.text: Which of the following correctly describes the contrary relation (A vs. E) in the modern square of opposition?

options.label: A
options.text: A and E cannot both be false.

options.label: B
options.text: A and E can both be false when the subject class is empty.

options.label: C
options.text: A and E cannot both be true.

options.label: D
options.text: A and E are contradictory in every interpretation.

questions.solution: Correct answer: A and E can both be false when the subject class is empty..

questions.text: Given the premises: (1) P ∨ Q (inclusive disjunction) and (2) P. Which conclusion is logically justified?

options.label: C
options.text: No conclusion about Q can be drawn.

questions.solution: Correct answer: No conclusion about Q can be drawn..

questions.text: Premise: “Every student read some book” (∀x∃y Read(x,y)). Conclusion: “There is a book that every student read” (∃y∀x Read(x,y)). Does the conclusion follow?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, the quantifiers can be swapped without changing meaning.

options.label: B
options.text: No, the premise allows each student a different book.

options.label: C
options.text: Yes, provided the domain of books is finite.

options.label: D
options.text: No, unless existential import is assumed for the universal.
